contributions.statement: Benchmark any 'feed errors back to the agent' repair loop against a blind redraw with the same attempt budget; here sanitized diagnostics added nothing over resampling (76.7% vs 76.7%), so spend effort on validators instead.
contributions.evidence: Table 3: C vs D +0.0pp (CI -12.2 to 13.3), 12/12 discordant; effective n ~35 repaired runs (audit); diagnostics only raised executability 100% vs 96.7%. One model, Python, thin diagnostics.

contributions.statement: Give the agent a frozen, machine-readable metadata card for each data source it queries (dimensions, codes, units); it nearly eliminated wrong-filter errors.
contributions.evidence: Table 2/4: exact correctness 27.8% -> 51.1% (cluster CI 8.9-37.8, Holm p=0.0049); wrong filters 39 -> 4.

contributions.statement: Before comparing agent configurations, specify the full output contract (ranking key, units, serialisation) in both prompt and scorer; an under-specified contract understated accuracy by 23.4 points and flipped a significance result.
contributions.evidence: Table 6: C 53.3% vs 76.7% under original vs specified contract; adjusted p 0.2153 vs 0.0013; between-run, post-hoc redesign (audit).

contributions.statement: Do not treat 'it ran and matched the schema' as correct: about one in five executable answers was silently wrong even in the best condition.

reason: The equal-budget redraw control is the cleanest test in the KB of whether diagnostics, not extra attempts, drive repair; the contract-completeness effect is a usable evaluation-hygiene rule. Single model and Python limit it to indirect transfer.
